domains.label: Platform
domains.purpose: Run by Sakalya: plans, billing clinics, feature rollout, support, platform analytics. Console only.

domains.label: Identity
domains.purpose: People who sign in, their sessions and devices. One user can belong to many clinics.

domains.label: Clinic setup
domains.purpose: The clinic itself: branches, domains, rooms, modules, roles, staff memberships, numbering.

domains.label: Patients and doctors
domains.purpose: Each clinic's own patient records, identifiers, families, referral sources and practitioners.

domains.label: Scheduling
domains.purpose: Appointments, their history, and the walk-in token queue.

domains.label: Clinical
domains.purpose: Visits, notes, vitals, diagnoses, prescriptions, procedures, treatment plans, files and specialty data.

domains.label: Clinic operations
domains.purpose: Lab work, inventory and stock, equipment maintenance, payroll and consultant fees.

domains.label: Money
domains.purpose: Price list, bills, payments, refunds, expenses and daily cash closing.

domains.label: Notifications
domains.purpose: Templates, rules, consent, recalls, campaigns, promo codes, the outbox and every message sent.

domains.label: Websites
domains.purpose: Generated clinic websites, their versions, booking requests and traffic.

domains.label: Trust and audit
domains.purpose: Patient consents, who viewed what, every change, and data-rights requests.

domains.label: Onboarding
domains.purpose: First-login progress and data imports from old software.

tables.name: plans
tables.purpose: Subscription plans clinics can buy (Solo, Clinic, Pro, Enterprise).

tables.name: features
tables.purpose: Every feature that a plan can include or limit.

tables.name: plan_features
tables.purpose: What each plan includes, and its limits.
tables.notes: Primary key (plan_id, feature_id).

tables.name: subscriptions
tables.purpose: Which plan a clinic is on and whether it is paid up.

tables.name: saas_invoices
tables.purpose: Sakalya's own GST invoices to clinics for the subscription.

tables.name: entitlement_overrides
tables.purpose: Per-clinic exceptions to the plan: promos, grandfathering, custom deals.

tables.name: usage_counters
tables.purpose: How much of each limited feature a clinic used this month.
tables.notes: Primary key (org_id, feature_id, period). Incremented by the API and worker.

tables.name: feature_flags
tables.purpose: Switches that release a feature gradually, separate from plans.

tables.name: flag_rules
tables.purpose: Who a flag is on for: named clinics, a percentage, a plan, a platform or app version.

tables.name: platform_users
tables.purpose: Sakalya staff who can use the console, and their role.

tables.name: support_grants
tables.purpose: Time-limited permission a clinic gives Sakalya support to look inside its data.

tables.name: announcements
tables.purpose: Release notes and notices shown inside the clinic apps.

tables.name: org_daily_stats
tables.purpose: Per-clinic daily counts for the console. Counts only, never patient data.
tables.notes: Primary key (org_id, day). Written nightly, copied to BigQuery.

tables.name: users
tables.purpose: Anyone who signs in: staff, doctors, patients, Sakalya staff.

tables.name: sessions
tables.purpose: Signed-in sessions, so a stolen phone or idle PC can be signed out.

tables.name: devices
tables.purpose: Phones and browsers a user signs in from, with push tokens.

tables.name: organizations
tables.purpose: A clinic business, the tenant. Everything clinic-owned points here.
tables.notes: Members can read only their own clinic's row. The console creates clinics through app.create_clinic().

cols.name: number_prefix
cols.note: 1 to 3 capital letters: SC in SC-1042

tables.name: branches
tables.purpose: Locations of a clinic. Single-location clinics have one.

cols.name: gstin
cols.note: when the branch has its own GST registration

cols.name: state_code
cols.note: GST state code, e.g. 27 for Maharashtra; the place of supply

tables.name: org_domains
tables.purpose: Host names that resolve to a clinic: its portal and its website.
tables.notes: Read before the clinic is known, through app.resolve_host(); cached in memory for a short time.

tables.name: slug_history
tables.purpose: Old slugs, so renamed clinics, doctors and pages keep redirecting.

tables.name: rooms
tables.purpose: Chairs, rooms and labs that appointments can be booked into.

tables.name: org_modules
tables.purpose: Specialty modules switched on for a clinic, with their settings.

cols.name: settings
cols.note: e.g. tooth numbering FDI or Universal

tables.name: org_settings
tables.purpose: One row per clinic: branding, bill and prescription settings, defaults.
tables.notes: Primary key (org_id): exactly one row per clinic.

tables.name: assets
tables.purpose: Non-medical files: logos, signatures, generated PDFs, website images.
tables.notes: Stored in a different bucket from patient attachments.

tables.name: permissions
tables.purpose: Every permission the API checks, such as patients.read.
tables.notes: Seeded by migrations from the Rust permission list; a test checks that they match.

tables.name: role_templates
tables.purpose: Default roles copied into each new clinic: owner, doctor, front desk, assistant, finance.

tables.name: role_template_permissions
tables.purpose: The permissions each default role starts with.
tables.notes: Primary key (role_template_id, permission).

tables.name: roles
tables.purpose: Named bundles of permissions. Seeded from templates; owners can add their own.

cols.name: key
cols.note: owner, doctor, consultant, finance, front_desk, assistant, or custom

tables.name: role_permissions
tables.purpose: What a role may do: module.action plus a scope.
tables.notes: Primary key (org_id, role_id, permission).

cols.name: permission
cols.note: a key from permissions: patients.read, finance.view

tables.name: memberships
tables.purpose: A user's place in a clinic: role, branches, status. The link between users and clinics.
tables.notes: Unique (org_id, user_id): one membership per person per clinic. Before the clinic scope is set it is read only through app.authorize().

tables.name: membership_branches
tables.purpose: Which branches a staff member works at. No rows means every branch.
tables.notes: Primary key (org_id, membership_id, branch_id). Branch-scoped permissions read this table.

tables.name: invitations
tables.purpose: Pending invites to join a clinic.

tables.name: number_sequences
tables.purpose: Counters behind readable numbers: SC-1042, V-2026-0318, SC/26-27/000318.
tables.notes: Primary key (org_id, kind, series, period). app.next_number() issues a number with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... RETURNING in the caller's transaction, so the first number of a new year needs no setup. GST invoice numbers stay within 16 characters.

cols.name: kind
cols.note: patient, visit, invoice, prescription, receipt, lab_order, queue_token

cols.name: series
cols.note: main, a separate series such as one per GSTIN, or a branch for queue tokens

cols.name: period
cols.note: financial year such as 26-27 or a local date for queue tokens, in the clinic's time zone; or empty

tables.name: patients
tables.purpose: A clinic's own record of a patient. Two clinics never share this row.
tables.notes: A phone number is contact information, never identity: families share numbers and numbers change. A merge only sets merged_into_id; records stay on the original patient and reads resolve to the canonical one, so a wrong merge can be undone. Number, phone and name-prefix search use plain indexes; fuzzy name search goes through app.search_patients(), because trigram matching can't use an index under row-level security. Same-phone registrations get a duplicate warning, never an automatic merge.

cols.name: number
cols.note: SC-1042, unique per clinic, used in URLs

cols.name: search_name
cols.note: lower-case name kept by a trigger, for prefix search

cols.name: birth_date_estimated
cols.note: date_of_birth was estimated from an age

cols.name: merged_into_id
cols.note: set by a merge, cleared by an unmerge

tables.name: patient_identifiers
tables.purpose: Extra IDs for a patient: the clinic's file number, smart card, ABHA, legacy import.
tables.notes: Unique (org_id, kind, value).

tables.name: family_links
tables.purpose: Relationships between patients in the same clinic: parent, child, spouse, guardian.

cols.name: can_manage
cols.note: guardian may act for this patient

tables.name: referral_sources
tables.purpose: Where patients come from, for the finance and marketing filters.

cols.name: kind
cols.note: patient, doctor, online, walk_in, camp, insurance, other

tables.name: medical_history_items
tables.purpose: Patient-level history: past conditions, surgeries, long-term medicines, habits, family history.

cols.name: source
cols.note: clinician, assistant, patient, import, device, ai_draft, abdm

tables.name: patient_links
tables.purpose: Phase 3: connects a patient's own Aarogyam account to their record at each clinic.
tables.notes: This is the single-umbrella view: one person, many clinic records, joined only by verified links.

tables.name: practitioners
tables.purpose: Doctors who see patients at the clinic, with registration and fees.
tables.notes: Built in M3 with the columns the calendar needs. Planned: slug (public page), qualifications, council, signature_asset_id -> assets, default_fee_paise, is_visiting.

cols.name: membership_id
cols.note: null for a visiting consultant without a sign-in

tables.name: working_hours
tables.purpose: Weekly hours per clinic or doctor. Split shifts are two rows.
tables.notes: Replaced as a whole per doctor. Clinic hours and valid_from/valid_to are planned.

tables.name: leave_blocks
tables.purpose: Time a doctor is unavailable. Booking into it is allowed with a warning.

tables.name: appointments
tables.purpose: A booked slot with a doctor, optionally in a room or chair.
tables.notes: An exclusion constraint on (org_id, room_id, time range) for active rows (not cancelled, not no-show, not deleted) stops two bookings in one chair; a doctor in two chairs at once is a warning, not an error. Status changes follow the transition table in aarogyam_domain::schedule. Visits point at appointments, not the other way round.

cols.name: status
cols.note: booked, confirmed, arrived, in_chair, completed, cancelled, no_show

tables.name: appointment_events
tables.purpose: Every status change of an appointment, for history and no-show reports.

cols.name: changes
cols.note: {column: [old, new]} for times, room and doctor

tables.name: queue_tokens
tables.purpose: Walk-in tokens shown on the waiting-room screen.
tables.notes: Unique (org_id, branch_id, day, token_number) and one token per appointment. Numbers come from number_sequences (kind queue_token, series = branch, period = local date).

tables.name: teleconsult_sessions
tables.purpose: A video or audio consultation attached to an appointment.
tables.notes: Follows the 2020 Telemedicine Practice Guidelines; the prescription is issued in the usual way afterwards.

cols.name: room_ref
cols.note: the provider's room id, never a public link

tables.name: care_episodes
tables.purpose: A course of care spanning visits: a root canal on tooth 36, a pregnancy, a diabetes plan.
tables.notes: Optional: visits, treatment plans and specialty records may link to an episode. Built when a pack needs it.

tables.name: encounters
tables.purpose: One visit. Visit-level clinical data (complaint, vitals, notes, procedures, files) hangs off it.
tables.notes: Unique (org_id, id, patient_id): every child row carries patient_id and a composite foreign key (org_id, encounter_id, patient_id), so a visit's notes, vitals, procedures and files can't belong to another patient. Patient-level facts (allergies, active conditions, history) live on the patient and may be updated during a visit; they do not require one. Opening a visit writes access_log.

cols.name: clinician_id
cols.note: the member responsible; a doctor's practitioner record hangs off the same membership

cols.name: appointment_id
cols.note: foreign key added once appointments exist; one visit per appointment

tables.name: clinical_notes
tables.purpose: Doctor and intake notes. Signed notes never change.
tables.notes: Drafts are edited by their author only. Signing freezes the note: app.freeze_when() lets a signed or conflict note only move to entered_in_error (with a reason) and nothing else on it change. Never merged automatically: if a change synced from a device collides with a note already signed on the server, it is kept as a separate note with status conflict, linked by conflicts_with_id, and its author resolves it by marking one version entered_in_error. Corrections go in note_addenda.

cols.name: signed_by
cols.note: the author; only they may sign

cols.name: conflicts_with_id
cols.note: the version this one collided with during sync

tables.name: note_addenda
tables.purpose: Corrections and additions to a signed note, with their own author and time.

tables.name: observations
tables.purpose: Measurements: BP, pulse, temperature, SpO2, weight, height, sugar.
tables.notes: Values are never edited: a correction is a new row that supersedes the old one, which moves to corrected and stays visible. app.freeze_when() allows only final -> corrected or entered_in_error. A row with source ai_draft needs verified_by.

cols.name: kind
cols.note: bp_systolic, bp_diastolic, pulse, temperature, spo2, weight, height, blood_sugar

cols.name: value_num
cols.note: checked against a plausible range per kind and unit

cols.name: unit
cols.note: UCUM: mmHg, /min, Cel, [degF], %, kg, cm, mg/dL

cols.name: code
cols.note: LOINC code per kind, set by the server

cols.name: supersedes_id
cols.note: the value this one corrects (same patient and kind)

cols.name: source
cols.note: clinician, assistant, patient, import, device, ai_draft, abdm

tables.name: conditions
tables.purpose: Diagnoses and the problem list. Patient-level; a visit link records where it was found.

cols.name: display_text
cols.note: what the doctor wrote, always present

cols.name: flagged
cols.note: shown in the clinical flags banner while active

cols.name: source
cols.note: clinician, assistant, patient, import, device, ai_draft, abdm

tables.name: allergies
tables.purpose: Allergies, shown as a warning banner on the patient and on prescriptions.

cols.name: source
cols.note: clinician, assistant, patient, import, device, ai_draft, abdm

tables.name: drug_catalog
tables.purpose: Shared list of medicines (generic name, strength, form, usual dose) for quick prescribing.

cols.name: allergy_classes
cols.note: penicillin, nsaid ...; lets the allergy check match a class

tables.name: prescriptions
tables.purpose: A prescription from a visit: shown to staff and the patient, printed with the clinic letterhead.
tables.notes: Issued prescriptions never change (a trigger refuses): a correction cancels and reissues. The print shows the doctor's name, qualifications and registration number, generic names in capitals, the clinic's branding, and a small 'Prescribed with Aarogyam' footer with a QR code that opens the verified copy.

cols.name: number
cols.note: RX-412, assigned by the server when issued

cols.name: encounter_id
cols.note: visit; foreign key added after the visits branch merges

cols.name: override_reason
cols.note: why it was issued despite allergy alerts

cols.name: verify_token
cols.note: the QR's random token; opens only validity, date and clinic, so reprints keep it

cols.name: recipient
cols.note: patient name, number, age and sex at issue

tables.name: prescription_items
tables.purpose: One medicine on a prescription.

cols.name: drug_name
cols.note: as printed; generic name in capitals

cols.name: timing
cols.note: before_food, after_food, empty_stomach, bedtime, sos, as_directed

tables.name: procedures
tables.purpose: Treatment actually done (or planned for today) in a visit.
tables.notes: Done procedures are frozen by app.freeze_when() (only done -> entered_in_error). One live procedure per plan item. Marking done will deduct stock via procedure_materials and can create a lab_order.

cols.name: surfaces
cols.note: subset of M, O, D, B, L

cols.name: price_paise
cols.note: the fee; billing (M5) links it to the price list

cols.name: treatment_plan_item_id
cols.note: same patient; completing the procedure marks the item done

tables.name: treatment_plans
tables.purpose: A proposed course of treatment with a cost estimate, accepted or declined by the patient.
tables.notes: The estimate is the sum of its items that aren't cancelled, computed when read.

cols.name: encounter_id
cols.note: the visit it was proposed in

tables.name: treatment_plan_items
tables.purpose: Steps of a treatment plan, in phases.
tables.notes: Accepting a plan accepts the chosen items and cancels the rest. An item becomes done when its procedure is done; the plan is then in_progress, and completed when no item is left to do.

cols.name: surfaces
cols.note: subset of M, O, D, B, L

tables.name: attachments
tables.purpose: Patient files: photos, X-rays, reports, documents, audio, signed consent.
tables.notes: Served only through short-lived signed links (HMAC, 5 minutes) issued after a permission check; each download writes access_log. Local disk in development, object storage later, behind one Storage trait.

cols.name: kind
cols.note: photo, xray, report, document, audio, consent

cols.name: mime_type
cols.note: from the content: JPEG, PNG, PDF, DICOM

cols.name: source
cols.note: clinician, assistant, patient, import, device, ai_draft, abdm

tables.name: voice_notes
tables.purpose: A recorded note, its transcription status and the draft it produced.

tables.name: specialty_records
tables.purpose: Specialty Pack data as versioned JSON. Longitudinal: a tooth chart or pregnancy spans many visits.
tables.notes: Each change writes a new row and marks the previous current one superseded, so the full history (tooth 36: caries, filled, crown) is kept. A partial unique index keeps one current entry per tooth and surface; a crown, implant or missing tooth also supersedes that tooth's surface entries. app.freeze_when() allows only current -> superseded or entered_in_error.

cols.name: encounter_id
cols.note: the visit that changed it, if any

cols.name: data
cols.note: validated against the module's schema on write; dental: tooth, surface, finding, note

cols.name: surface
cols.note: generated from data.surface: M, O, D, B, L, or none for the whole tooth

cols.name: source
cols.note: clinician, assistant, patient, import, device, ai_draft, abdm

tables.name: document_templates
tables.purpose: Print and form layouts: prescriptions, bills, consent forms, certificates, letters.
tables.notes: Aarogyam's default layouts are copied into each clinic as data, so org_id is never null.

tables.name: prescription_alerts
tables.purpose: Safety warnings raised when a prescription was issued, and what the doctor did about them.
tables.notes: Overrides are kept with their reason for medico-legal review.

cols.name: kind
cols.note: allergy, interaction, contraindication, pregnancy, lactation, pediatric_dose, duplicate, precaution

tables.name: drug_interactions
tables.purpose: Licensed reference data: which medicines interact, how badly, and why.
tables.notes: Loaded from a licensed Indian drug database; contraindications and pregnancy categories sit alongside it.

tables.name: document_extractions
tables.purpose: Smart Scan: values read from a photographed paper report, waiting for confirmation.
tables.notes: Nothing enters observations until a person confirms it; confirmed rows carry source = import.

tables.name: consent_forms
tables.purpose: A signed procedure consent.

tables.name: lab_vendors
tables.purpose: Outside labs: dental labs for crowns, pathology, radiology.

tables.name: lab_orders
tables.purpose: Work sent to a lab, its due date and status.

tables.name: lab_payments
tables.purpose: Money paid to labs.

tables.name: suppliers
tables.purpose: Where materials are bought.

tables.name: inventory_items
tables.purpose: Materials and medicines the clinic stocks.

tables.name: stock_batches
tables.purpose: Received stock by batch, with expiry and cost.

tables.name: stock_movements
tables.purpose: Every change in stock: purchase, use, adjustment, expiry. Stock history comes from here.

tables.name: procedure_materials
tables.purpose: Materials a treatment uses, so stock deducts itself.

tables.name: equipment
tables.purpose: Chairs, autoclaves, X-ray units and their service schedule.

tables.name: maintenance_logs
tables.purpose: Services and repairs done on equipment, and when the next is due.

tables.name: salary_structures
tables.purpose: A staff member's monthly salary from a date.

tables.name: payroll_entries
tables.purpose: Salary paid for a month, with deductions and advances recovered.

tables.name: staff_advances
tables.purpose: Salary advances given to staff and how much is recovered.

tables.name: consultant_fee_rules
tables.purpose: How a visiting consultant is paid: a percentage or fixed amount per treatment.

tables.name: consultant_payouts
tables.purpose: Payments made to consultants for a period.

tables.name: price_items
tables.purpose: The clinic's price list. Seeded from the specialty, then edited.

cols.name: category
cols.note: consultation, preventive, endodontics, medicines …; drives the revenue mix

cols.name: sac_hsn
cols.note: SAC 9993 for health care, HSN for goods

cols.name: taxable
cols.note: false for health care by a clinical establishment (exempt)

tables.name: invoices
tables.purpose: A bill to a patient. Totals are stored at issue; whether it is paid is derived from allocations.
tables.notes: Issued bills never change (a trigger refuses): corrections void and replace. Numbers are never generated offline. Payment state (unpaid, partial, paid) is derived from payment_allocations of payments that are not void.

cols.name: number
cols.note: SC/26-27/000318, assigned by the server when issued (at most 16 characters)

cols.name: encounter_id
cols.note: visit; foreign key added after the visits branch merges

cols.name: place_of_supply
cols.note: state code; IGST when it differs from the branch's state

cols.name: supplier
cols.note: snapshot at issue: legal name, GSTIN, address, state

cols.name: recipient
cols.note: snapshot at issue: patient name and number

cols.name: replaces_invoice_id
cols.note: when a voided bill is reissued

tables.name: invoice_items
tables.purpose: Lines on a bill, each optionally tied to a price item or procedure. GST is computed per line at issue.
tables.notes: Lines change only while the bill is a draft.

cols.name: procedure_id
cols.note: foreign key added after the visits branch merges

tables.name: payments
tables.purpose: Money received from a patient, by any method.

cols.name: idempotency_key
cols.note: unique per clinic; a retry returns the first payment

cols.name: request_hash
cols.note: a reused key with a different request is refused

tables.name: payment_allocations
tables.purpose: Which bills a payment pays, so advances and partial payments work.
tables.notes: A trigger refuses allocations past the bill's balance or the payment's amount, and to bills that are not issued.

cols.name: patient_id
cols.note: must match both the payment's and the bill's

tables.name: refunds
tables.purpose: Money returned to a patient.

tables.name: expense_categories
tables.purpose: Rent, electricity, salaries, consumables and so on.

tables.name: expenses
tables.purpose: Money the clinic spends.

tables.name: daily_closings
tables.purpose: End-of-day cash count against what the system expects.

tables.name: message_templates
tables.purpose: Message text per channel and language. Clinic rows override platform defaults.
tables.notes: org_id is null for platform defaults; this table allows that.

tables.name: notification_rules
tables.purpose: When to message: on an event, before an appointment, on birthdays, on recalls.

tables.name: contact_preferences
tables.purpose: Per patient and channel: may we message them, and was promotional consent given?
tables.notes: Primary key (org_id, patient_id, channel).

tables.name: recalls
tables.purpose: Follow-ups that are due: cleaning in six months, BP review, vaccine.

cols.name: source_procedure_id
cols.note: foreign key added after the visits branch merges

tables.name: audiences
tables.purpose: Saved patient filters for campaigns: age, sex, treatment, doctor, fees, history.

tables.name: campaigns
tables.purpose: A one-off or scheduled send to an audience: health tips, offers.

tables.name: promo_codes
tables.purpose: Discount codes a clinic can share.

tables.name: promo_redemptions
tables.purpose: Each use of a promo code on a bill.

tables.name: outbox_events
tables.purpose: Messages to send because of a change, written in the same transaction as the change, for the worker to deliver.
tables.notes: Guarantees a message is never lost or sent for a change that rolled back. The worker claims due rows across clinics with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED through app.outbox_claim, retries with backoff, gives up after 5 attempts, and deletes rows 30 days after processing.

cols.name: recipient
cols.note: a staff address; patient messages will carry the patient's id in the payload

cols.name: payload
cols.note: ids and non-patient template values, never patient details

cols.name: secret
cols.note: a one-time link secret, cleared once sent or abandoned

cols.name: next_attempt_at
cols.note: when due, or when a worker's lease ends

tables.name: messages
tables.purpose: Every message scheduled or sent, with its outcome and cost.

cols.name: status
cols.note: scheduled, queued, sent, delivered, read, failed, skipped

tables.name: message_events
tables.purpose: Delivery receipts from providers: sent, delivered, read, failed.

tables.name: notifications
tables.purpose: The in-app notification feed for staff.

tables.name: sites
tables.purpose: A clinic's generated website: template family, repository and live version.

tables.name: site_versions
tables.purpose: Each publish of a site, so any version can be restored.

tables.name: booking_requests
tables.purpose: Booking requests from the website, before they become appointments.

tables.name: site_daily_stats
tables.purpose: Website visits and bookings per day, for the clinic and the console.
tables.notes: Primary key (org_id, day). Imported from Cloudflare Web Analytics.

tables.name: consents
tables.purpose: A patient's permission for a clinic or doctor to see records held elsewhere, for a purpose and time.
tables.notes: Every grant and revocation is audited. The clinic owns its record; the patient controls sharing across clinics.

tables.name: share_links
tables.purpose: Expiring links that let a patient open a prescription, bill or report on the clinic's host.
tables.notes: Typed, tenant-aware foreign keys instead of a generic resource id: a check constraint requires exactly the column matching resource, so a link can only ever open a record of the same clinic and patient. Every open is written to access_log with purpose patient_self.

cols.name: token_hash
cols.note: the link holds a 256-bit token; only its hash is stored

cols.name: pin_hash
cols.note: SHA-256 of token and the six-digit PIN printed on the paper

cols.name: failed_attempts
cols.note: five wrong PINs lock the link

tables.name: access_log
tables.purpose: The access record: who opened which patient record, why, when and from which device. Patients can see it.
tables.notes: Primary key (org_id, at, id), partitioned by month. No foreign keys, so the ledger never blocks erasure and adds no lock cost; the ids refer to users, patients, devices and share_links. Append-only: the app role can insert but never update or delete. Views made offline are queued on the device and uploaded.

cols.name: actor_user_id
cols.note: null when a patient opens a share link

cols.name: share_link_id
cols.note: when opened through a share link

cols.name: resource
cols.note: chart, note, attachment, prescription, invoice, export

cols.name: purpose
cols.note: care, front_desk, billing, support, patient_self, export

tables.name: audit_events
tables.purpose: The change history: every insert, update and delete, written by triggers.
tables.notes: Primary key (id, at), partitioned by month; org_id is null for platform tables. Written by app.audit_row(), which skips updates that change nothing and records only metadata for inserts into append-only tables. No foreign keys.

cols.name: changes
cols.note: changed columns only, as {column: [old, new]}, masked per audit_config

tables.name: audit_config
tables.purpose: Per table: which columns the audit trigger leaves out or masks.

cols.name: mask
cols.note: recorded as changed with the value hashed, e.g. pin_hash

cols.name: metadata_only
cols.note: record only that the row changed

tables.name: data_requests
tables.purpose: Patients' DPDP requests: export, correction, erasure.

tables.name: onboarding_progress
tables.purpose: Where a new clinic is in the first-login wizard, and its answers.
tables.notes: One row per clinic.

tables.name: imports
tables.purpose: A data import from Excel or old software.
tables.notes: M3 imports CSV text sent in the request and records only committed imports; uploads from files, appointments and invoices are planned.

cols.name: mapping
cols.note: our field to the file's column

tables.name: import_rows
tables.purpose: Each row of an import with its result, so failures can be fixed and retried.

cols.name: row_number
cols.note: line in the file, header is 1

steps.what: Clinic created on a trial plan with its subdomain.
Owner accepts the invite and becomes a member with the owner role.
Specialty, branding, prices and hours set up from defaults.
Site generated from answers, repository created, built and deployed.
